goal: Fix one production defect: browser/control-server.ts retains the collector's live Chromium page after collection ends, so a finished/cancelled xe.gr tab kept consuming ~1 CPU and the hosted container's entire 1.5GiB for hours. Correct the real server/session lifecycle in strict TypeScript. Terminal completion, cancellation (active or idle, including cancelling a CAPTCHA pause), and non-human-verification failure must stop the managed page's document activity without deleting cookies/profile, stored listings, checkpoints, exports or history. Keep a genuine CAPTCHA/human-verification page and the same context available until explicit verification/resume or cancellation. Do not close the externally owned hosted browser or unrelated tabs. Hold the collection lock until bounded cleanup settles; cleanup rejection must not wedge later requests, overwrite the primary collection result/error, or leave unhandled rejection. A subsequent allowed collection must get a usable page/session; preserve persisted cancellation, Retry-After and all prior behavior/tests. Cover real createServer and compiled module paths with offline regression tests that fail on the baseline and pass after the fix. Include real owned local Chromium with a local fixture showing that document activity stops after completion/cancel while a CAPTCHA remains available and a later run works; no live xe.gr traffic and no personal profiles. Run final root npm ci and npm run check in the same fresh external copy excluding node_modules,dist,.git and all .atoma-prefixed paths before copying, preserving file modes; install browser test dependencies separately only if needed for the offline Chromium proof. Keep Vite/build layout and unrelated parser/migration code unchanged. No deployment or collection on production; app is deliberately stopped. Deliver a minimal reviewed correction, not broad refactoring.
acceptanceCriteria: Terminal collection paths stop managed page activity, preserve human-verification sessions and durable data, and allow safe reuse; offline regressions prove it.
